routes.name: Visa-free entry
routes.summary: Citizens of about 157 countries can enter without a visa. Most get 30 days. You need a passport valid 6 months past departure and an outbound ticket within 30 days.

other: Most listed nationalities get 30 days. Brazil and Israel get 59 days.
Indian passports get 14 days, extendable by 7. Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR passports get 14 days.
Passport valid at least 6 months after you leave
Outbound ticket leaving within 30 days of arrival (Indians need a return or onward ticket)
Check the full list on the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs site for your passport

stay.note: To stay past 30 days, get a Temporary Visitor visa at an embassy before you fly, or extend at the Bureau of Immigration in the Philippines.

routes.name: eTravel arrival registration
routes.summary: A free online arrival form. It is not a visa. You show the QR code before boarding your flight.

other: Free to register
The embassy page gives a 72 hour timing rule. Confirm the exact window on the official eTravel site before flying.

sources.label: Philippine Embassy Lisbon, visa-free entry and eTravel

routes.name: 9(a) Temporary Visitor Visa
routes.summary: The regular tourist and business visit visa for people who are not visa-free. You apply at a Philippine embassy or consulate. It covers pleasure, business, and some other short visits.

other: Passport valid 6 months past your exit date
Return flight ticket or itinerary
Posts may ask for bank statements, an invitation letter, or a visa for the country you are applying from
Fees and processing times differ by embassy. Check your local post.

stay.note: Single entry is valid 3 months. Multiple entry visas are valid 6 or 12 months.

routes.processing: Dubai post says single entry takes at least 8 working days and multiple entry at least a month. Other posts differ.

sources.label: Philippine Consulate General Dubai, visa page
Philippine Consulate General Sydney, visa information

routes.name: 9(b) Transit Visa
routes.summary: For people traveling through the Philippines to another country. Stay is limited to 72 hours.

other: Rules for airside transit without a visa were not confirmed on an official page

sources.label: Philippine Consulate General Dubai, visa page

routes.name: 9(f) Student Visa
routes.summary: Visa for foreign students at Philippine schools. It needs authority from the Department of Foreign Affairs. Full requirements were not confirmed.

other: Requirements and fees not confirmed from an official page. Ask your nearest Philippine embassy.

sources.label: Philippine Consulate General Dubai, visa page

routes.name: 9(g) Pre-Arranged Employment Visa
routes.summary: Work visa for foreigners with a Philippine employer. It needs authority from the Department of Foreign Affairs and may need an interview. Other rules were not confirmed.

other: Alien Employment Permit rules and fees not confirmed from an official page. Check the Bureau of Immigration and the Department of Labor and Employment.

sources.label: Philippine Consulate General Dubai, visa page

routes.name: 13(a) Non-Quota Immigrant Visa (spouse or child of a Filipino)
routes.summary: Immigrant visa for the husband or wife, or unmarried child under 21, of a Philippine citizen. Probationary period and fees were not confirmed.

other: Proof of relationship, Filipino spouse's birth certificate and passport, financial capacity affidavit, police clearance, medical certificate
Filipino spouse may be called for an interview
Some nationalities need approval from Manila
Probationary period not confirmed. Check the Bureau of Immigration.

documents: Marriage certificate or proof of relation
Filipino spouse's PSA birth certificate and passport page
Notarized letter from the Filipino spouse
routes.processing: Tehran post says 3 to 4 weeks after a complete application is accepted. Other posts differ.

routes.name: Special Resident Retiree's Visa (SRRV) Classic
routes.summary: A retiree visa run by the Philippine Retirement Authority. You park a deposit and pay an annual fee. Applicants must be 40 or older.

income.note: Pension proof for a single applicant. USD 1,000 per month with dependents.

investment.note: Visa deposit, pensioner age 50+. Pensioner 40-49: USD 25,000. Non-pensioner 50+: USD 30,000. Non-pensioner 40-49: USD 50,000.

other: Dependents are a legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21

routes.name: SRRV Courtesy (former Filipinos)
routes.summary: A cheaper SRRV for former Filipinos who naturalized elsewhere and have not reacquired Philippine citizenship.

other: Former Filipino citizen who naturalized in another country

routes.name: SRRV Courtesy (foreign nationals)
routes.summary: SRRV for retired diplomats, officers of international organizations, some retired military, and high achievers or philanthropists. Deposit amounts were hard to read on the page.

other: Deposit shown as USD 1,500 at 50+ and USD 3,000 or 6,000 at 40-49, but the table was unclear. Confirm with the Philippine Retirement Authority.
Annual fee shown as USD 100 for principal plus 2 dependents, USD 10 per extra dependent

routes.name: Dual citizenship under RA 9225
routes.summary: Former natural-born Filipinos who naturalized abroad can retake Philippine citizenship by oath and keep their other citizenship. Unmarried children under 18 are included.

other: Must be a former natural-born Filipino who acquired foreign citizenship by naturalization
Foreign spouses and children 18 and over cannot use this route
Birth certificate, petition form, 3 photos and a valid ID

citizenship.note: Oath of allegiance, then an Identification Certificate from the Bureau of Immigration. Full civil and political rights, with limits for public office.

sources.label: Philippine Embassy Brussels, dual citizenship FAQs
